assertion_analysis.fails_if: Restore SESSION_TMP_ROOT=/dev/shm; the independent /tmp expectation reddens, as final-negative-control.log demonstrates.
Ignore the configured scratch root, choose a memory path, share an allocation directory between sessions, change private mode, or fail valid starts.

Report nonzero empty-session use, omit busy allocated blocks, report the empty session, choose the smaller directory or misaggregate totals; total-versus-row is a consistency assertion supported by the independent 20480-byte lower bound, not independent size evidence alone.
Allow /dev/shm directly or through a symlink instead of raising.

Fail the sample, undercount the known nonempty file, disagree between stdout and persisted data, omit either session path, misattribute the duty or omit its directory/alert; stdout-versus-file is transport consistency, supported independently by >=16384.
Launch or create scratch at the configured half-disk cap, omit the busy duty, or retain the refusal after deleting the measured file; the cap is derived from independent file stat blocks.
Follow either symlink, swallow walk PermissionError, emit numeric zero rather than unknown, return success on unreadability, omit alert or publish a false health reading.
Remove the elapsed-time bound or stop raising TimeoutError after the controlled clock crosses 15 seconds.
Change stated defaults, ignore host overrides, or accept a zero disk share.

Break the health command or omit/alter the scratch subprocess value in the TSV; injected 12345 checks transport, not disk measurement, and reverting the real sampler alone would survive this transport-only assertion.

Fail publication, omit the busy duty, lose the independent largest-directory path, diverge direct/published reason or command, or leak a duty to empty/unrelated conversations; parity checks are consistency checks rather than proof of reason semantics on their own.
Fail resampling or retain the busy duty in either production view after deleting the file.

findings.text: blocking: _scratch_disk duplicates the mount-table parsing and longest-prefix filesystem classification owned by reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:1741 (_mount_table) and :1769 (_path_is_tmpfs); it neither wraps nor extends that owner, so mount parsing and filesystem policy can drift independently; expose or extend the existing owner and keep the session-specific allowed-filesystem policy on that shared mechanism.
